title: Israel recovers the body of Ran Gvili, the last hostage held in Gaza
body:
On Monday 26 January 2026, Israel identified and returned the body of Master Sgt. Ran Gvili, 24, the last hostage held in Gaza, the Times of Israel reported. Gvili was a police officer in the Yasam counter-terror unit who was killed fighting Hamas at Kibbutz Alumim on 7 October 2023. He was the last of the 251 people kidnapped that day still held in Gaza, 843 days later, and his return meant that no hostages remained in Gaza for the first time since 2014.

The Israel Defense Forces searched the al-Batash Muslim cemetery in the Shejaiya neighborhood of Gaza City on specific intelligence. Troops and forensic experts, including 20 dentists, tested about 250 exhumed bodies before a dental match confirmed his identity. The report said a captured Palestinian Islamic Jihad operative provided information and that Hamas confirmed information to Israel through mediators. Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem said the discovery showed its commitment to the ceasefire while accusing Israel of violations.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said "we brought everyone back" and that the next phase was disarming Hamas and demilitarizing Gaza, not reconstruction. President Isaac Herzog said no Israeli hostages remained in Gaza. The October 2025 ceasefire had required release of all hostages within 72 hours, but deceased hostages were returned intermittently over about two months. Israel was to hand over at least 15 Palestinian bodies to Gaza's Health Ministry, following the usual ratio of 15 to one.
